one_liner: Case manager for Prince William County residents with developmental disabilities, coordinating services, supports, and Medicaid waiver care plans. The position is grant-funded.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, ease with the public, and government-client consulting at IEM transfer well to client and family relationships. DD service coordinator roles in Virginia usually require a human services degree and experience working with people with developmental disabilities, and nothing on file shows either. The posting excerpt is truncated, so the full qualifications must be checked before deciding.
eligibility: Open the full posting and read the minimum qualifications. Virginia DD case managers typically need a human services degree, or an equivalent, plus experience with people with developmental disabilities.
Check whether the role requires DBHDS DD case manager competencies or training to be completed within a set period after hire.
Expect a background check, and possibly a driver's license with a clean record for home and community visits.
The position is grant-funded, so confirm how long the funding lasts and whether the job is benefits-eligible.
strategy: Before investing time, get the full minimum qualifications from governmentjobs.com. Apply only if your degree and experience meet them or a stated substitution is allowed.
Present your IEM work as coordinating services for vulnerable populations, for example disaster survivors or community stakeholders, but only if that is what you actually did.
Highlight public-facing skills that match the role: building rapport, explaining complex programs in plain language, and connecting people to resources.
Include any volunteer, caregiving, or advocacy experience with people who have disabilities, since that directly matches the posting's mission.
Answer the supplemental questions thoroughly with concrete examples, because county HR often screens on those answers.
Apply well before the November 12, 2026 close.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [type of services/resources] for [number] [clients/communities] affected by [disaster/program] while working at IEM, serving as the primary contact for [stakeholders].
Built working relationships with [agencies/families/officials] to resolve [issue], resulting in [outcome].
Documented [cases/plans/reports] in [system] to meet [government client/regulatory] requirements.
interview_questions: How would you build trust with an individual with a developmental disability and their family during a first meeting?
Describe a time you coordinated multiple providers or agencies to meet someone's needs.
How do you manage a large caseload and documentation deadlines?
What does person-centered planning mean to you?
watch_outs: The role likely requires a human services degree and DD-specific experience that Daniel may not have.
Because the position is grant-funded, job security depends on continued funding.
Case management may involve fieldwork, home visits, and emotionally demanding situations.
The pay range is wide, and someone without direct experience will likely start near the bottom of it.
